Monks at a Phetchaburi temple give their Loy Krathong sermon from a spaceship

Yes, a spaceship (well, a replica), and the temple has a pretty good reason for it

Share

Spotted at a Phetchaburi temple this Loy Krathong, a UFO with monks on board. While the rest of us are lighting candles and hoping our banana-leaf krathong doesn’t sink straight away, one local wat swaps its usual pulpit for a spaceship.

Wat Bandai Thong in Ban Kum subdistrict holds its Thet Mahachat sermon on November 23-24, with monks reciting the story of Prince Vessantara from the replica craft. A heads-up online beforehand tells followers they’re going to space this year, but not to worry.

It sounds like a stunt, but the reasoning is quite sweet. In a Facebook post, the temple says the spaceship stands for a journey with no limits, like the Buddha’s teachings, which still reach people around the world thousands of years on. A new look doesn’t change the religion, it adds. It’s about getting younger people curious enough to come along.

As the temple sees it, a spaceship can fly you to faraway planets, but the Buddha’s teaching takes your mind somewhere even better, to peace and freedom from suffering. One is just a machine people built, while dharma carries wisdom.

The temple dates back to 1732 and sits on a bend of the Phetchaburi River, an easy day trip from Bangkok. Nearly 300 years old, and still the most futuristic temple in town.
